title: Scalar extension of ordinary cohomology to the algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and interpret $\Qlb$-objects in the algebraically closed coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], whose coefficient complexes form the stagewise category $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $F_\ell$ be the global geometric Frobenius [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] on $\RGamma(X,(\Ql)_X)$ and $F_{\Qlb}$ the one on $\RGamma(X,(\Qlb)_X)$, and let $H^i(X,\Ql)$, $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ be the ordinary cohomology groups of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. For every integer $i$, the canonical map

$$
H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\longrightarrow H^i(X,\Qlb),
$$

induced by the scalar-extension functor (the object $(\Ql,\RGamma(X,(\Ql)_X))$ of the stagewise category represents $\RGamma(X,(\Qlb)_X)$), is an isomorphism of $\Qlb$-vector spaces, and it carries $F_\ell|_{H^i(X,\Ql)}\otimes1$ to $F_{\Qlb}|_{H^i(X,\Qlb)}$. In particular, for $0\leq i\leq2d$, the operator $F_{i,\ell}\otimes1$ on $V_{i,\ell}\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb$ of [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] and the operator $F_{\Qlb}$ on $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ are conjugate by a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism; hence they have the same eigenvalues with the same algebraic multiplicities, and $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})=\det(1-TF_{\Qlb}\mid H^i(X,\Qlb))$ in $\Qlb[T]$.

proof.text: Put $K=(\Ql)_X$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $C=\RGamma(X,K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X*}K)$. The canonical constant Weil object at $\Qlb$ is represented by $(\Ql,(K,\theta_{\Ql}))$, so its underlying object is $(\Ql,K)$ by [def-weil-constant-weil-structure]. The common-stage convention for the direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and the explicit stagewise point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] give $Ra_{X*}(\Ql,K)=(\Ql,Ra_{X*}K)$ and $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\Ql,Ra_{X*}K)=(\Ql,C)$. Thus, by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $\RGamma(X,(\Qlb)_X)$ is the object $(\Ql,C)$ of the point coefficient category. This identifies the representative used in the statement without taking a tensor product of sheaves with an infinite coefficient field.

source.place: statement, ordinary cohomology after scalar extension; expand the common-stage coefficient conventions at the finite stage E=Ql

proof.text: For every $i\in\mathbf Z$, [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules] defines the cohomology of the pair $(\Ql,C)$ to be $\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb$. Since $\mathrm H^i(C)=H^i(X,\Ql)$ by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], this gives an isomorphism $\xi_i:H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(X,\Qlb)$. At the chosen stage it is the identity on this displayed tensor product; in a complex model after scalar extension its formula is $[z]\otimes b\mapsto[z\otimes b]$. The natural and tower-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension], together with the tensor tower identification in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], gives the same map if a larger finite coefficient stage or a different complex representative is used. It is therefore the canonical comparison induced by scalar extension, for every integer i.

source.place: statement, scalar-extension identification; its degreewise meaning in the stagewise coefficient category

proof.text: Write $\tau_K:\RGamma(X,K)\to\RGamma(X,Lg_X^*K)$ for ordinary Frobenius transport [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. It is the composite of the point transport $\iota_{Ra_{X*}K}$ and the point functor applied to $\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,*}(K)$. For the representative $(\Ql,K)$, [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] explicitly represents the first map over $\Ql$, and [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] explicitly represents the second over the same field. Apply the stagewise point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. In its target category $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, let $J_{\Ql}$ be the stage functor of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], using its scalar-extension unit isomorphisms to identify stage arrows with their representatives. Composition there is composition over a common field, so $\tau_{(\Ql,K)}=J_{\Ql}(\tau_K)$. By [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], the constant Weil map is represented by $\theta_{\Ql}$; hence $\RGamma(\theta_{\Qlb})=J_{\Ql}(\RGamma(\theta_{\Ql}))$. Consequently the defining composite of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], interpreted at this common stage, gives $F_{\Qlb}=J_{\Ql}(\RGamma(\theta_{\Ql}))\circ J_{\Ql}(\tau_K)=J_{\Ql}(\RGamma(\theta_{\Ql})\circ\tau_K)=J_{\Ql}(F_\ell)$. This checks the transport arrow as well as the Weil-structure arrow, with the geometric Frobenius convention fixed throughout.

source.place: statement, eigenvalue on ordinary cohomology after scalar extension; compute both arrows in the global geometric Frobenius composite at its field of definition

proof.text: Apply the cohomology functor of [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules] to the equality in Step 3. Under $\xi_i$, a morphism represented by $f$ over $\Ql$ acts by $\mathrm H^i(f)\otimes1$: for a chain-map representative the formula is $[z]\otimes b\mapsto[f(z)]\otimes b$, by naturality in [lem-weil-cohomology-commutes-scalar-extension] and the tensor-map formula in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. To check arbitrary derived morphisms, write $\eta_C:\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_{\Ql}\Qlb)$ for that lemma's isomorphism. For a chain map $u:C\to D$, naturality reads $\eta_D(\mathrm H^i(u)\otimes1)=\mathrm H^i(u\otimes1)\eta_C$. If u is a quasi-isomorphism, the lemma makes $u\otimes1$ a quasi-isomorphism too. Multiplying this equality by the inverse cohomology maps gives $\eta_C(\mathrm H^i(u)^{-1}\otimes1)=\mathrm H^i(u\otimes1)^{-1}\eta_D$. The equality is also preserved by composition. Since the derived category is the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], these equations establish naturality on its morphisms, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. With $f=F_\ell$, it follows that $F_{\Qlb}\xi_i=\xi_i(\mathrm H^i(F_\ell)\otimes1)$. These are exactly the induced actions on the cohomology groups in [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius].

source.place: statement, Frobenius-equivariant scalar extension; expand the induced morphism on cohomology

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq2d$, [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] identifies $V_{i,\ell}$ with $H^i(X,\Ql)$ and $F_{i,\ell}$ with $\mathrm H^i(F_\ell)$. The space is finite-dimensional by [prop-cohomological-finiteness], applied to the constant Weil sheaf with $E=\Ql$ and the given smooth proper geometrically connected $X_0$. Thus Step 4 proves $F_{\Qlb}=\xi_i(F_{i,\ell}\otimes1)\xi_i^{-1}$ on $H^i(X,\Qlb)$, the required conjugacy. If $(v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ is a $\Ql$-basis of $V_{i,\ell}$, [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] makes $(v_j\otimes1)$ a $\Qlb$-basis; its image under $\xi_i$ is a basis of $H^i(X,\Qlb)$. If $F_{i,\ell}v_j=\sum_r a_{rj}v_r$, equivariance gives $F_{\Qlb}\xi_i(v_j\otimes1)=\sum_r a_{rj}\xi_i(v_r\otimes1)$. The two operators over $\Qlb$ therefore have exactly the same matrix A, and A is the coefficientwise image of the original matrix over $\Ql$.

source.place: statement, final eigenvalue assertion; identify the smooth-proper cohomological family and choose the corresponding tensor and transported bases

proof.text: Use the bases of Step 5. By [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial], the two $\Qlb$-operators have the same characteristic polynomial $\det(U I_n-A)$. An eigenvalue means a scalar $\lambda$ with a nonzero vector v satisfying $Fv=\lambda v$; the equation is carried in both directions by the invertible map $\xi_i$, so their eigenvalues agree. Their algebraic multiplicities, the root multiplicities of this common characteristic polynomial [def-weil-root-multiplicity], agree as well. By [def-weil-reverse-characteristic-polynomial] and [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant], both reverse characteristic polynomials over $\Qlb$ are $\det(I_n-TA)$. Moreover the permutation formula $\det B=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_j B_{\sigma(j),j}$ commutes with coefficient inclusion $\Ql\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, since a ring homomorphism preserves each finite product and sum. Thus $\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid V_{i,\ell})$, read in $\Qlb[T]$, equals $\det(1-TF_{\Qlb}\mid H^i(X,\Qlb))$. When n=0 the empty product is 1, and the assertions about eigenvalues and multiplicities are empty, so this argument includes zero cohomology spaces.
